content: No man undertakes a trade he has not learned, yet everyone thinks himself qualified for the hardest of all trades—that of living well.
author: Socrates
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Socrates's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
